sections.heading: 3. History of Present Illness / Current Episode

paragraphs.label: Primary reason for treatment
paragraphs.text: The patient reports nightmares almost every night and startle responses to loud noises since returning from a six-year army service, along with recent suicidal thoughts.

paragraphs.label: Precipitating / contextual factors
paragraphs.text: The patient served in the army for six years and returned with the onset of nightmares and startle responses.

paragraphs.label: Functional impact
paragraphs.text: The patient has been thinking about killing themselves and has a handgun in the bedroom closet, though the patient has not taken it out and does not intend to use it because of their daughter.

paragraphs.label: Narrative / additional details
paragraphs.text: The patient reports a prior suicide attempt in 2018 involving a bottle of pills and a three-day hospital stay, and currently drinks six beers most nights. The patient agrees to give the handgun to their brother and to start a partial hospitalization program and prazosin for nightmares.
The patient reports experiencing nightmares almost every night and startles at loud noises, indicative of trauma symptoms.

paragraphs.text: The patient keeps a handgun in the bedroom closet and has considered using it. The patient plans to give the gun to their brother.

The provider recommended a partial hospitalization program starting the next day for the patient's safety concerns. The provider also suggested starting prazosin one milligram at bedtime to address the patient's nightmares. It was discussed that the patient should give the handgun key to the wife that night or store the gun outside the home. The patient agreed to give the gun to their brother the next day. A safety plan was made with the crisis line, 988.
